title: Learning-Augmented Streaming Algorithms for Approximating Boolean Max-CSPs
claim: Streaming algorithms track a few simple counters over vertex partitions by degree and predicted label, which is enough to estimate the objective.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right, rectangle split by vertical line and dashed horizontal line
description: A single black-and-white schematic shows a large rectangle. A solid vertical line splits it into a narrow left region labeled H (high-degree vertices) and a wide right region labeled L (low-degree vertices). A dashed horizontal line splits the whole rectangle into an upper half (predicted +1) and a lower half (predicted −1). The corner labels L+ (top right) and L− (bottom right) mark the low-degree vertices in each half. On the left, a black dot labeled v is a high-degree vertex. Four arrows connect v to the L+ and L− regions: two point toward v and two point away. They are labeled X_{L+,v}, X_{v,L+}, X_{v,L−} and X_{L−,v}. In the right region, arrows labeled X_0 (downward), X_1 (rightward, twice) and X_2 (upward) show the counters for edges within L. The eye goes first to the dot and its fanning arrows.
caption: Illustration of the counters maintained in the algorithm for Max-Dicut. The rectangle represents the vertex set $V$, partitioned into high-degree vertices $H$ (left) and low-degree vertices $L$ (right). We also partition $V$ by the predicted labels (indicated by the horizontal dashed line): the upper region contains vertices predicted as $+1$ (denoted by "$+$"), and the lower region contains vertices predicted as $-1$ (denoted by "$-$").
abstract: We study learning-augmented streaming algorithms for estimating the value of Boolean Maximum Constraint Satisfaction Problems (Max-CSPs). Specifically, we consider streaming algorithms equipped with an $\varepsilon$-accurate oracle: for each variable, the oracle outputs a label in $\{-1,1\}$ that agrees with a fixed optimal assignment with probability $1/2+\varepsilon$, and disagrees otherwise. Prior work by Dong, Peng, and Vakilian [ITCS 2025] showed that, for the special case of Max-Cut, such an oracle enables a $(1/2+Î©(\varepsilon^2))$-approximation using $\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon)$ words of space in insertion-only streams, and $\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon,\log n)$ words of space in dynamic streams. We substantially generalize and strengthen their result, provided that a highly accurate estimate of $\varepsilon$ is available. For any Boolean Max-$2$CSP and any $Î·>0$ independent of $\varepsilon$, we obtain, with high constant probability, a single-pass $(1-Î·)$-approximation using $\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon,1/Î·)$ words of space in insertion-only streams, and $\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon,1/Î·,\log n)$ words of space in dynamic streams, where $n$ is the number of variables. We further extend our techniques to general Boolean Max-$k$CSPs for $k\ge 3$, with slightly worse space complexity.
